security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD never defines, reads, or writes CSR 0x107 (sivt). If firmware or a prior boot stage leaves sivt.EHV=1, synchronous exceptions are hardware-vectored to stvec + (cause << 2). FreeBSD stvec points to a single cpu_exception_handler with no vector table padded around it, so vectored exceptions land on arbitrary instructions in the surrounding code, causing immediate undefined behavior.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: absence of csr_write(sivt, 0) or csr_clear(sivt, EHV) in locore.S or trap initialization; absence of CSR_SIVT / SIVT_EHV macro definitions in riscvreg.h or encoding.h
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD RISC-V port is completely unaware of CSR 0x107 (sivt) and its EHV bit; if firmware leaves EHV=1, synchronous exception vectoring redirects traps to unmapped code offsets around the single-entry handler, crashing the kernel

findings.finding: CSR_SIVT (0x107) is not defined. The CSR number space jumps from CSR_SCOUNTEREN (0x106) to CSR_SSCRATCH (0x140), skipping 0x107 entirely. No DECLARE_CSR(sivt, ...) exists. This means no code in the kernel can possibly read, write, or clear the SIVT register.

No SIVT_EHV or any SIVT-related bit definitions exist in riscvreg.h. The csr_write/csr_set/csr_clear helper macros are defined here, but without CSR_SIVT and SIVT_EHV constants, no code can issue csr_clear(sivt, SIVT_EHV) to disable EHV.

findings.finding: Boot path writes stvec (0x105) four times (lines 212, 232, 369, 387) but never writes or clears CSR 0x107 (sivt). If firmware set sivt.EHV=1, exceptions will be vectored to stvec+(cause<<2). stvec is set to cpu_exception_handler address with bit 0 = 0 (direct mode), but the EHV bit in sivt is independent — EHV=1 enables hardware vectoring even without stvec[0]=1. No csr_write or csr_clear of 0x107 at any point in the boot sequence.
findings.snippet:
la    t0, cpu_exception_handler
        csrw  stvec, t0

        /* Ensure sscratch is zero */
        li    t0, 0
        csrw  sscratch, t0

findings.finding: cpu_exception_handler is a compact single-entry dispatch routine (6 instructions). It is not a vector table — there are no padded .align entries with exception dispatch stubs at stvec+0x08, +0x10, +0x18, ... offsets. If vectored exceptions are enabled (via sivt.EHV=1), exceptions whose cause >= 1 will land on arbitrary instructions in surrounding .text (cpu_exception_handler_user at +8, or other code), causing undefined behavior.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_exception_handler)
        csrrw  sp, sscratch, sp
        beqz   sp, 1f
        j      cpu_exception_handler_user
1:
        csrrw  sp, sscratch, sp
        j      cpu_exception_handler_supervisor
END(cpu_exception_handler)

findings.finding: Trap handling C code never reads or writes stvec (0x105) or sivt (0x107). No runtime check or mitigation for EHV-vectored exceptions is performed. The only CSR accesses are csr_read(sstatus) for SPP/SIE/SUM assertions.
